Indicator 3 measures the proportion of adult patients with Crohn's disease who undergo a colonoscopy within one year following an ileocecal resection, evaluated across national, regional, and departmental levels in Denmark [^src1]. In the 2024 reporting period, the national average stood at 65%, with 117 out of 179 eligible patients receiving the procedure [^src1]. 

Because this comparison is based on a single dated section from 2024, no temporal trends or year-over-year changes can be assessed. 

At the regional level, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] emerged as a leader, achieving an 83% compliance rate (33 out of 40 patients) [^src1]. Conversely, the Capital Region (Hovedstaden) trailed significantly at 49% (28 out of 57 patients) [^src1]. The remaining regions fell between these extremes, with Zealand (Sjælland) at 74%, Central Denmark (Midtjylland) at 69%, and North Denmark (Nordjylland) at 55% [^src1].

Departmental data reveals stark contrasts and notable outliers. EGS Esbjerg Medicinsk Mave og Tarm Amb. achieved a perfect 100% rate (9 out of 9 patients), making it one of the most successful departments alongside [[ouh-odense-medicinsk-mave-tarm-afd-s|OUH Odense Medicinsk Mave-Tarm Afd. S]], which reached 83% (15 out of 18 patients) [^src1]. Rigshospitalet also reported a 100% rate, though its exact patient count is masked and the wide confidence interval (3-100%) indicates a very small sample size [^src1]. On the lower end, Herlev Mave-, Tarm- og Leversygd. is a major outlier, recording only a 17% rate (with masked patient counts and a 0-64% confidence interval) [^src1]. Nordsjælland Kirurgisk Afdeling also struggled, reaching only 38% (3 out of 8 patients) [^src1]. While no explicit clinical target or threshold is defined in the dataset, the source summary identifies the 83–100% range as the benchmark for the most successful institutions [^src1].
